audit_findings.title: Completed growth capex may be embedded permanently in the anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: $410.1 million FY2026 total capex; growth-versus-maintenance portion unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Nonrecurring growth capex deducted in calculating the $241.4 million OE anchor would depress every forecast year's OE and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: We have completed our capital growth initiatives, opening our new facility in Argentina to serve the growing Latin America market, and reduced structural capital intensity, lowering capital expenditures by $240.6 million from the prior year, to $410.1 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates completed expansion projects but does not demonstrate that their expenditures were separated from maintenance capex in OE. This is material because the $410.1 million capex pool is 170% of anchor OE. At the existing DCF factors, an anchor increase of approximately $295.6 million would bring BASE value to the $49.87 price, while approximately $213.6 million would do so in BULL. The FY2027 capex outlook of $380-$410 million indicates substantial continuing requirements, but it does not establish the economically recurring maintenance amount.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the FY2026 project-level capex ledger; classify expansion, modernization, environmental compliance, replacement, and maintenance spending; normalize recurring capex; and rerun all scenarios without changing growth or discount-rate inputs.

audit_findings.title: Restructuring costs have a normalization and timing mismatch
audit_findings.magnitude: $111.6 million FY2026 pre-tax Plan charges ($63.3 million cash, $48.3 million non-cash, and $98.1 million after tax); $80-$110 million disclosed FY2027 closure charges with at least $16-$22 million of cash expenditure implied at the range endpoints
audit_findings.mechanism: Retained one-time FY2026 charges depress anchor OE and value, while omitted FY2027 closure cash expenditures overstate the equity bridge or near-term OE.
audit_findings.evidence: In connection with the planned facility closure, we expect to incur total pre-tax charges of approximately $ 80 million to $ 110 million, substantially all of which are expected to be recognized in our fiscal year ending May 30, 2027.
audit_findings.explanation: The charges are filed, but their treatment in the $241.4 million anchor is unresolved. If the full $98.1 million after-tax FY2026 amount remained in OE, it equals 40.6% of the anchor and is plainly material. Conversely, the FY2027 closure creates a separate senior cash use that should not be ignored or capitalized as a perpetual expense.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile each FY2026 charge to the OE calculation, identify amounts already added back through non-cash adjustments, normalize only demonstrated one-offs, separately deduct the expected FY2027 cash outflow once, and rerun the valuation.

audit_findings.title: Consolidated earnings may include income belonging to the Austrian minority owner
audit_findings.mechanism: Failure to allocate the Austrian venture's results to its 25% outside interest would mismatch consolidated OE with value attributed solely to Lamb Weston common shares; profits would overstate value and losses would understate it.
audit_findings.evidence: In addition, we own a 75% interest in a joint venture in Austria.
audit_findings.explanation: The 75% ownership and consolidation are demonstrated, but the record supplied does not show the venture's earnings, noncontrolling-interest presentation, profit-allocation terms, or amounts removed from OE. A valuation error is therefore possible but neither its existence nor materiality is established.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the Austrian venture's annual financial statements, ownership and profit-allocation agreement, noncontrolling-interest roll-forward, and distributions; reconcile the outside owner's share for every OE year and rerun if it was omitted.

audit_findings.title: The cash bridge includes cash already committed to a dividend
audit_findings.magnitude: $52.2 million, equal to approximately $0.36 per diluted share and 1.6% of BASE equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge adds May 31 cash even though the recorded dividend payable consumed that cash after year-end for holders determined before the valuation date.
audit_findings.evidence: On June 5, 2026, we paid $ 52.2 million of dividends to stockholders of record as of the close of business on May 8, 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated timing error if the $68.2 million balance was carried unchanged to September 5. Removing $52.2 million lowers BASE value from $22.68 to approximately $22.32 per share and BULL value from $26.68 to approximately $26.32, leaving both far below the $49.87 market price; it therefore does not change the valuation conclusion by itself. The September 4 dividend and intervening cash generation still require a proper roll-forward.
audit_findings.action: Replace the May 31 cash amount with an actual or reconstructed September 5 cash balance reflecting the June 5 and September 4 dividend payments, intervening operations, financing, capex, and repurchases.

audit_findings.title: Unreserved antitrust claims could create a senior cash claim
audit_findings.mechanism: Defense costs enter OE, while any uninsured settlement or judgment is a senior contingent cash claim deducted from the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: The relief sought in the complaints includes treble damages, injunctive relief, equitable monetary relief, pre- and post-judgment interest, costs and attorneys’ fees.
audit_findings.explanation: The pending actions and requested treble damages are demonstrated, but the filing states that no potential-loss range can presently be estimated. The supplied record provides no damages base, probability, insurance recovery, or settlement information, so neither a reliable deduction nor materiality determination can be made. Absence of a reserve does not establish zero economic exposure.
audit_findings.action: Obtain current pleadings and procedural status, counsel's exposure assessment, alleged commerce and damages estimates, insurance limits and exclusions, indemnities, and defense-cost forecasts; then model a separately identified probability-weighted bridge deduction if supportable.

audit_findings.title: The annual anchor contains an extra operating week
audit_findings.magnitude: $28.9 million filed Segment Adjusted EBITDA benefit; OE effect unquantified; a full dollar-for-dollar OE sensitivity is approximately $2.13/$2.66/$3.14 per share in BEAR/BASE/BULL
audit_findings.mechanism: An unnormalized 53rd-week contribution would inflate recurring anchor OE and all forecast and terminal cash flows.
audit_findings.evidence: The fiscal years for the Consolidated Financial Statements presented consist of a 53-week period for fiscal 2026 and 52-week periods for fiscal 2025 and 2024.
audit_findings.explanation: The 53-week fiscal year is demonstrated, but failure to normalize the OE calculation is not. As a conservative sensitivity, treating the entire $28.9 million EBITDA benefit as recurring OE lowers scenario values to approximately $16.12, $20.02, and $23.54 per share. Those values remain well below the $49.87 price, so the current valuation conclusion is unchanged. Actual OE impact should be smaller or offset in part by taxes, capex, and working-capital normalization.
audit_findings.action: Trace whether the anchor components were already converted to 52 weeks; if not, remove the extra week's after-tax operating contribution and associated working-capital and capex effects, then rerun the scenarios.
